ended: Lost the East Semifinals 0-4 to NY

archetype.name: Overachiever (Maxey-carried)
archetype.definition: A team whose margin said break-even but whose record, after a 24-58 collapse, landed in the playoffs, where it upset the division-champion Celtics before New York ended it.

report.headline: A break-even team by margin that rode Maxey past Boston, then hit New York

recap.finish: 45-37; won the East 1st Round 4-3 over BOS, lost the East Semifinals 0-4 to NY
recap.body:
This was a middle-of-the-league team that played its way into a meaningful spring. The ratings are almost perfectly level: a 115.4 ORtg and a 115.5 DRtg, a -0.1 Net Rtg that ranked 18th, and a full-season point differential of -15. The offense ranked 17th and the defense 16th. A point differential like that implies 41 wins. Philadelphia won 45, and the +4 W vs Pt Diff, third-highest in the league, is the gap. A year after going 24-58 with a -6.3 Net Rtg, though, getting to even was real progress, not a mirage.

The season never had a defining surge or collapse. A 4-1 October gave way to a 6-8 November that left them 10-9. From there they stayed modestly above .500 every month: 7-5 in December, 10-7 in January (the best month), 6-5 in February. March was the soft spot. At 8-8, the defense allowed 118.63 a game, its worst stretch since November. The longest winning streak was five games and the longest losing streak four, which tells you how little the team swung. The closing run was mixed, with a 6-4 last ten that hid a 2-3 finish against tougher opponents like Detroit, San Antonio and Houston.

The team ran on Tyrese Maxey and on not wasting possessions. Maxey made All-Star and All-NBA Third Team, posting 1,980 points, 8.7 Win Shares and a 5.4 BPM over 2,661 minutes, and he ranked 4th among point guards. The backcourt graded B+, the team's only good group. Philadelphia's 11.9 TOV % ranked 6th and its 13.3 Opp TOV % ranked 8th, so it usually won the possession game. It also got to the line (27.5 FT Rate, 11th). The shooting was below average: 34.9 3P % and a 53 eFG %, both under the league. Behind the guards the roster thinned out. The wings graded C and the frontcourt D+. Joel Embiid (38 games, +7.6 On-Off) and Paul George (37 games, +4.4 On-Off) were the two most impactful players after Maxey, and each missed more than half the season. The defensive glass was a steady leak, with a 72.5 DRB % that ranked 26th.

The first round turned this into a season worth remembering. Boston, the 56-26 division champion, won Game 1 by 32 at home. The Sixers stole Game 2 in Boston, then lost both home games, the second 128-96. Facing elimination three times, they won all three, including Game 7 in Boston 109-100. New York then took the series in four games, starting with a 137-98 blowout and ending 144-114 in Philadelphia. Only Game 2 was close. Across the postseason they were outscored by 109 points with a -10.6 Net Rtg. The opponents' 56.2 Opp eFG % and a 20.1 ORB % (15th of 16) show a team that was outshot and outrebounded once the opponents got better.

The takeaway is a decent team with one star-level engine, not a contender. The Boston series showed what the Maxey-Embiid-George trio can do when all three play. The rest of the year showed how often they didn't, and how little the wings and bigs offer when they don't.

highlights.title: Maxey carried the whole operation
highlights.body: Maxey led the team in minutes, points and Win Shares by a wide margin. He paired a 29.4 USG % with 58.8 TS %, efficient volume, and earned All-NBA recognition. With Embiid and George each out for more than half the season, his production is the main reason the record held above .500. In the playoffs his efficiency dipped but held up (56.2 TS %, 2.8 BPM).

highlights.title: Erasing a 1-3 deficit against Boston
highlights.body: Down three games to one to the 56-26 Celtics, Philadelphia won three straight elimination games, two of them in Boston. It was the clearest proof of what this core can do when its stars are on the floor. Embiid posted a 6 BPM in his seven playoff games.

highlights.title: Winning the turnover battle
highlights.body: A 6th-ranked TOV % and an 8th-ranked Opp TOV % gave the Sixers extra possessions most nights. That edge offset below-average shooting. Taking care of the ball held up in the playoffs (11.5 TOV %, 3rd of 16), so it looks like a real trait of a guard-led team.

lowlights.title: Stars missed more than half the season
lowlights.body: Embiid played 38 games and George 37, and they had two of the best On-Off marks on the roster (+7.6 and +4.4). In their absence, a frontcourt built around Barlow, Bona and Drummond graded D+. The team's ceiling depends almost entirely on how often those two play.

lowlights.title: The record outran the margin
lowlights.body: A -15 point differential implies 41 wins, not 45. The +4 W vs Pt Diff ranked third in the league, and close-game edges like that rarely repeat. Net Rtg ranked 18th, the same spot the team holds on the site's rankings. This was a .500-quality team in true terms.

lowlights.title: Glass and size exposed by New York
lowlights.body: A 72.5 DRB % (26th) was a season-long weakness. In the playoffs it spread to both ends of the floor: 38 rebounds a game (15th of 16) and a 20.1 ORB %. New York won by 39 and 30 in two of the four games, part of a -109 postseason differential.

arc.note: After a 4-1 start and a 6-8 November, the Sixers stayed a few games over .500 every month, sagged defensively in March, and peaked with the Boston comeback before New York swept them.

recap.nextYear: Maxey is the foundation: an All-NBA guard on a B+ backcourt with efficient high volume. The guard rotation alongside him logged heavy minutes, with Edgecombe a positive On-Off despite a 54 TS % and Grimes the steadier shooter. The obvious needs are the C wings and the D+ frontcourt, which is graded well behind the guards whenever Embiid isn't playing. Defensive rebounding was 26th and broke down further in the playoffs. Expect some regression from the +4 close-game edge: a -0.1 Net Rtg team usually wins in the low 40s, not 45. The real gain was the jump from a -6.3 Net Rtg to break-even. Whether it climbs further mostly depends on Embiid and George playing far more than the 38 and 37 games they managed..

confidence.note: Full 82-game season plus 11 playoff games; star availability clouds the true talent read
